title: The Silent Fold
logline: When a legendary paper engineer visiting Oak Creek Elementary is replaced by an impostor, a ten-year-old deaf boy uses his sharp eye for microexpressions to expose the fraud before the school's fundraiser money disappears.

beats.title: The Golden Ticket
beats.summary: Reyansh sits in the back of the bustling art room, holding his prized purple paper fortune-teller. He wants to win the District Art Showcase by getting this exact totem signed by the legendary paper engineer Charles Vance, who is speaking at the assembly today.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh has profound bilateral hearing loss. He is deaf. He navigates the noisy room visually, focusing on the vibrant colors and the geometric folds of his paper.

beats.title: The Goal and the Noise
beats.summary: Reyansh tries to show his work to Mrs. Gable, but she is distracted by the chaotic setup. Reyansh wants the signature for his own artistic validation, not to show off or teach others.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh observes the room's chaotic energy through vibrations and quick shifts in people's posture, reading their faces to understand the schedule.

beats.title: The False Welcome
beats.summary: The school gathers in the auditorium. The guest speaker, Charles Vance, is introduced. The crowd cheers, and the presentation screen flickers to life with a video about paper engineering.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh watches the video presentation which has visible captions enabled. He notices the real Charles Vance in the video has very specific, fluid hand movements.

beats.title: The Micro-Lie
beats.summary: The speaker on stage begins his presentation. While the other kids listen to the grand stories of adventure, Reyansh watches the speaker's face and notices a rapid twitch in his left cheek whenever he mentions his famous designs.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh reads the speaker's microexpressions, detecting a mismatch between the speaker's confident tone and his anxious, asymmetrical facial movements.

beats.title: The Clumsy Hands
beats.summary: The speaker attempts a simple paper fold on stage. He fumbles with the corners. Reyansh looks down at his own paper fortune-teller, knowing a master engineer would never crease paper with such clumsy force.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh's visual-spatial intelligence, sharpened by his primary reliance on sight and ASL, allows him to spot the technical errors in the speaker's hand movements.

beats.title: The Dismissal
beats.summary: Reyansh tries to alert Mrs. Gable using his notepad, pointing out that the man on stage is lying. Mrs. Gable patronizingly tells him to just sit back and enjoy the show, assuming he is simply confused.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh experiences the frustration of being talked down to and left out of the plan because the hearing teacher assumes his deafness limits his understanding.

beats.title: The Mockery
beats.summary: Two classmates, Leo and Sam, notice Reyansh trying to sign to Mrs. Gable. They make fake, exaggerated hand gestures to mock him, laughing among themselves.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh faces the vulnerability of hearing kids pretending to sign, but he maintains his focus on the unfolding mystery instead of letting them derail him.

beats.title: The Backstage Trail
beats.summary: Reyansh notices a man in a dark jacket whispering to the speaker from the wings, holding a heavy metal briefcase. Reyansh slips out of his seat to investigate backstage.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh moves silently and uses his heightened peripheral vision to follow the suspicious man without being detected.

beats.title: The Locked Closet
beats.summary: Backstage, Reyansh hears a faint, rhythmic tapping from the utility closet. He slides his paper fortune-teller under the door frame to test for movement, and someone grabs it from the other side.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh uses his tactile sensitivity to feel the vibrations of the tapping, leading him directly to the real Charles Vance who is trapped inside.

beats.title: The Expose
beats.summary: Reyansh frees the real Charles Vance, who is tied up. Together, they rush to the stage just as the principal is about to hand over the giant charity check to the impostor.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh signs rapidly to the real Vance, establishing an instant connection through clear visual communication.

beats.title: The Trap and the Triumph
beats.summary: The impostor tries to run with the check, but Reyansh pulls the master lever for the stage curtains, trapping the fake speaker in the heavy velvet folds. The police arrive.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh's quick visual assessment of the stage mechanics allows him to execute the perfect trap without needing to yell for help.

beats.title: The Signature
beats.summary: The real Charles Vance thanks Reyansh and signs his purple paper fortune-teller. Reyansh stands proud, his deaf identity unchanged, holding the key to his artistic future.
beats.trait_in_play: Reyansh stands with his purple hearing aid visible, celebrated by the Deaf community and his school alike, exactly as he was at the start.

trait_causality_note: Reyansh's ability to read microexpressions, developed through his visual focus as a deaf boy, allows him to identify the impostor speaker when all hearing characters are deceived by the spoken presentation.
